title: The Real History of 'Bug' and 'Debugging'
explainer: The word 'bug' for a technical fault predates computers by decades: Thomas Edison used it in an 1878 letter describing faults in his own inventions, reflecting slang already circulating among engineers and telegraph operators. The famous story of a moth taped into a 1947 Harvard Mark II logbook under 'First actual case of bug being found' is real, and that logbook now sits in the Smithsonian, but the handwriting in that entry is unidentified, and historians doubt it was written by Grace Hopper herself — whose real contribution was retelling the story for decades afterward, which helped cement 'debugging' in everyday programming vocabulary.

resources.title: Did Grace Hopper really invent the term 'bug' to describe software errors?
